subject: SIG: SSO/SCIM/RBAC - follow-up and evidence pack
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechco.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security.team@fintechco.com
Date: 2025-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SIG: Clarification on access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Hi Dev,

We're working through Redwood's SIG questionnaire and need a few clarifications on your access control controls for our security review:

- SAML: Can you confirm which NameID/attributes you expect (email vs persistent)? Any specific NameID format required?
- SCIM: Does your SCIM endpoint implement PATCH for group membership updates? Do you support nested groups and what rate limits exist?
- RBAC: List out default roles and whether custom roles are supported. How do you enforce least privilege for service accounts?
- MFA: Is MFA enforced for admin users and what factors are allowed (TOTP, hardware keys)?

Could you also provide screenshots/exports showing role mappings, SAML metadata, and a sanitized admin user list? We're on a tight timeline for our SOC 2 evidence collection.

Thanks,
Asha Reddy
Security Engineer, FintechCo
asha.reddy@fintechco.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Clarification on access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Hi Asha,

Thanks for the detailed list — we can provide everything you've requested. High level answers up front so your team can move while we collect artifacts:

- SAML: We support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML. Preferred NameID is email (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress) but we accept persistent identifiers if required. Required attributes: email, givenName, familyName, groups (optional).
- SCIM: Our SCIM 2.0 endpoint supports PATCH and PUT for user/group changes; group provisioning (including nested group handling) depends on the IdP mapping — we can share our expected schema. Typical rate limits are 300 req/min by default (configurable for Dedicated/Private customers).
- RBAC: Default roles are Viewer, Editor, Admin. We support custom roles via API/Console with fine-grained route permissions. Service accounts use scoped API tokens with no UI access and are constrained by role binding policies.
- MFA: MFA is required for all accounts with write/admin privileges. We accept TOTP (Authenticator apps) and hardware security keys (FIDO2/U2F).

I'll loop in Marissa and Stephanie to pull the SAML metadata, role mapping export, and a sanitized admin user list. I opened a HubSpot ticket for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/ticket/FintechCo/FT-4392.

Talk soon,
Dev
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG: Clarification on access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Hi Asha — attaching the artifacts we discussed. See brief notes below for each item.

[Attachment: redwood_saml_metadata.xml (application/xml)] — Our current SAML metadata. NameID defaults to email; we support both emailAddress and persistent formats. Assertion contains attributes: email, givenName, familyName, groups. Example NameID in our test tenant: "alice@example.com".

[Attachment: scim_endpoint_config.txt (text/plain)] — SCIM config: SCIM v2.0, endpoint https://scim.redwood.ai/v2, supports PATCH/PUT/GET, authentication via OAuth2 client_credentials + mTLS for higher assurance customers. SCIM accepts group members as array of values and will process IdP-provided group nesting if the IdP flattens groups prior to provisioning. Typical provisioning latency observed: < 60s for user updates.

[Attachment: admin_role_matrix.csv (text/csv)] — Export of role definitions and route-level permissions from our console. Default roles: Viewer (read-only), Editor (write to app-level resources), Admin (full access incl. billing). Custom roles: supported via API and limited in console to prevent privilege escalation. Service accounts are created with API-only tokens and are excluded from UI-permission flows.

[Attachment: mfa_policy_export.json (application/json)] — Shows policy that enforces MFA for any account with Admin, Billing, or Editor role with write access to sensitive settings. Allowed factors: TOTP (recommended) and WebAuthn/FIDO2 hardware keys.

Notes on least privilege: role bindings are additive and scoped to projects/accounts. We recommend creating dedicated service accounts with the minimum set of role bindings and rotating API tokens every 90 days (we provide a token rotation API).

If you want a SAML assertion example, see the included saml-assertion-example.xml in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence (link above).

Cheers,
Marissa

Subject: Re: SIG: Clarification on access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA)

Hi Asha — quick follow-up to answer the two items you called out and to include the sanitized admin list you requested.

1) Nested groups: Our SCIM implementation accepts group membership arrays and will ingest group objects as provided by the IdP. If the IdP sends nested group references we recommend flattening on the IdP side into explicit membership values; behavior for nested group expansion is IdP-dependent. For our standard managed IdP integrations (Okta, Azure AD) nested group sync is handled via the IdP SCIM connector and we have sample mappings we can share.

2) Custom roles: Yes, we support custom roles. They can be created via the Console (Admin -> Roles) or via the Roles API. Custom roles are composed from a set of granular permissions (route/action pairs). We have guardrails that prevent assignment of certain highly sensitive permissions to non-admin roles without an approval step.

Attached: sanitized_admins_export.csv (redacted email + role + created_at) and evidence_access_log.pdf (redacted) showing the export operation timestamp and the account that performed it.

[Attachment: sanitized_admins_export.csv (text/csv)]
